hero.headline: Premium Coffee
hero.sub: from the foothills of the Himalayas
hero.intro:
At Mewa Valley Coffee, we specialise in bringing you exceptional specialty coffee grown in the hills of Nepal.

We work closely with our dedicated sourcing team in Nepal to discover outstanding coffees from farmers across the country. 

By carefully selecting each coffee for its quality, character, uniqueness and sustainability, we connect Nepali farmers with coffee enthusiasts around the world.
hero.alt: Cloud moving across a forested ridge in the hill districts of eastern Nepal, a dirt road cut into the slope

premise.title: Why Nepal?
premise.body1:
Nepal is best known for being home to the world's tallest mountains. Yet among the hills below the Himalayas grows a wide variety of truly exceptional coffee

Nepali farmers grown their coffee at elevations between roughly 800 and 1,600 metres where it is allowed to ripen slowly in the cool air. Monsoon rain provides a powerful water supply whilst the steep, well drained slopes keep the roots from sitting wet.

The unique climate of Nepal's Himalayan foothills allow the coffee a longer period of maturation. Sugars and acidity build up in the beans, resulting in rich coffee with sweet and delicate notes.

coffee.title: What we offer
coffee.body1:
We are a UK based company with a dedicated team in Nepal. We source the very best of Nepali coffee, working with trusted and reputable producers. Our coffee goes through a rigorous quality testing and certification process before being delivered to your doorstep.

We source only premium 100% Arabica beans, primarily Bourbon and Typica. These traditional varieties, combined with Nepal’s distinctive geography and climate, provide the foundation for coffees with clarity, sweetness and lively acidity. 

Nepali coffee represents huge untapped potential, yet is very highly regarded by the specialty coffee community. The Eastern region in particular has gained a reputation for producing coffee of exceptional and outstanding quality. 

Nepali coffee from this region has repeatedly scored above 85 on the 50-100 SCA scale, as reported by trade magazines.

To give an example, in 2020, Nepali Coffee scored 92 in a blind assessment review by Press House Coffee (Californian Trade Magazine), highlighting it as "delicate, balanced and sweet-toned".

Our mission is twofold. We want to bring you the best of Nepali coffee and share with the world this truly exceptional product. We also assist the farmers, ensuring they are paid a truly fair share of profits, and are able to improve and develop their infrastructure.

All coffee that we import goes through very rigorous testing procedures, both at source in Nepal and here in the UK where we have a dedicated lab to assess each sample before it is passed on to the roaster.

about.title: About us
about.aboutBody1:
My name is Tom. I started this business with my wife Shriti. My interest in Nepali coffee began from the very first time I visited the country, where I was visiting my in-laws.

One of the first things I noticed from visiting the cafes in Kathmandu, Pokhara and Biratnagar was the exceptional quality of the coffee, and the care and enthusiasm taken in preparing it, which went way beyond what I was used to in the daily chain coffee I was drinking back in my hometown of London, UK.

At the time, I brought back some roasted beans from a local cafe and shared them among friends and family back in the UK, who all shared with me how good the coffee was. I had assume Nepal would be a primary sourcing country in the coffee world alongside Ethiopia, Columbia and Jamaica, yet was surprise to find out it is relatively unknown in the UK coffee world, despite the exceptional quality of the product.

In July of 2026 I came back to Nepal with the express purpose of visiting some farms, talking to farmers, hearing their stories and seeing the coffee growing process in action. What I discovered, was truly exceptional. The coffee we were served at the farms was some of the best I have ever tasted. Grown in the hills with care and true enthusiasm, many of the farmers we spoke to told us that growing the coffee had a significant positive impact on their lives.

I believe by bringing Nepali coffee to the UK, we can bring coffee lovers a new and high quality product as well as helping farmers reach their potential and beyond.
about.sourcingBody1: We are in active conversation with several producers at different stages of readiness, from established exporters to farms shipping their first commercial lots. They span the hill districts of Koshi: Solu, Bhojpur, Dhankuta and Ilam.
about.hillAlt: Hills near Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.mapAlt: Map of Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.sourcingBody2: Between them our producers work across washed, natural and yellow honey processing. Predominantly Arabica, with some Robusta at lower altitude in parts of Koshi Province.
about.sourcingBody3: Growing altitudes run from roughly 800 to 1,600 metres. Higher up, the cherry ripens slowly — sugars concentrate and the bean comes out denser.
